title: Cottage Pie
subtitle: British minced beef and vegetable pie with mashed potato crust
excerpt: The definitive British comfort dish: a rich, deeply savory mince of beef, carrots, onion, and celery in a thick gravy, topped with a generous layer of buttery mashed potato baked to a golden crust.

recipe.sourceNotes: Cottage pie is a British baked mince dish with a mashed potato topping, distinct from shepherd's pie only in its use of beef rather than lamb. The dish dates to at least the eighteenth century when the potato became a common food. The name originally referred to the modest rural cottage dwelling associated with the working classes who could afford beef mince but not cuts. The mince filling is built on a classic mirepoix of onion, carrot, and celery, thickened with flour and enriched with beef stock and Worcestershire sauce for depth. The potato topping is piped or spooned over and baked until a golden crust forms. It is an excellent make-ahead dish; the assembled pie keeps refrigerated for up to two days before baking.

content.text: Brown the mince in batches rather than crowding the pan; if the pan is too full, the meat steams rather than browns and the filling lacks colour and depth. The mashed potato should be firm enough to hold its shape on top without sinking into the filling; avoid over-adding milk or cream.

items.preparation: peeled and cut into chunks; for the topping

content.text: Heat the oil in a large, deep frying pan over high heat. Add the beef mince in two batches and brown thoroughly; about 4 minutes per batch. Remove the first batch while cooking the second.
Return all the mince to the pan. Add the onion, carrot, celery, and garlic. Cook over medium heat for 8 minutes until the vegetables are soft. Stir in the tomato puree and flour. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add the stock, Worcestershire sauce, bay leaves, and thyme. Bring to a simmer. Season and cook uncovered for 25 to 30 minutes until the sauce is thick. Preheat the oven to 200°C / fan 180°C / gas 6.
Boil the potatoes until tender. Drain and steam dry. Mash with butter and warm milk until smooth. Season well.
Transfer the mince to a large baking dish. Spoon the mash evenly over the top and rough up with a fork. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the top is golden and the filling is bubbling at the edges.
